purpose: Before/after comparison for PR #122 (batch per-mention embeddings + share embedder) -- same 3 questions, same eval DB, re-profiled after the fix
honest_finding: The fix's embedding-specific win is real and proven directly: embed_calls dropped ~4.6x (one batched embed_texts() call instead of ~4.6 individual embed_text() calls per turn) and embed_seconds dropped 1.3-1.8x across all 3 questions. BUT the average TOTAL wall-clock speedup was ~0.95x (no net win, and q3 was 33% SLOWER overall) because the 'other' stage (extraction/bookkeeping, not embedding or graph merges) roughly doubled between the before and after runs.
root_cause_of_other_stage_inflation: NOT a regression from this fix. Store.fetch_noun_labels() (store.py:919) runs 'SELECT label FROM noun' with no WHERE clause, no LIMIT -- a full-table scan, called once per turn write (provider.py:1049), scaling with the database's TOTAL cumulative noun count, not anything scoped to the current turn/session/owner. The eval DB grew ~1,400+ rows between the before and after profiling passes (my own repeated runs), making every subsequent turn's fetch_noun_labels() call slower -- unrelated to the embedding batching fix. Filed as github.com/rubyrayjuntos/hermes-memory#123. This means a 3-question sample profiled early in a run (as both rounds here were) cannot predict the true cost of later questions in a 500-question run, where the noun table grows continuously across ~250,000 turns -- the full run is likely considerably slower than naive extrapolation suggests, independent of this fix.
recommendation: PR #122 (batch embeddings + share embedder) is a real, proven, worthwhile fix on its own terms (4.6x fewer embed calls, less memory pressure) and should merge regardless. But do NOT use these total-wall-clock numbers to project the full 500-question run's duration -- issue #123's full-table-scan bug is likely the bigger lever at that scale and should be assessed/fixed first, or the full run's timing will be a surprise.
